newsitem.title: USA: Chemicals traffic restricted on lower Mississippi.
newsitem.headline: Chemicals traffic restricted on lower Mississippi.

text.p: Some shipping restrictions remained in place Monday on the Mississippi River after the river's crest surged past New Orleans over the weekend, officials said.
Northbound compressed gas and chemicals shipments were restricted to daylight travel from marker 78 below New Orleans to marker 235 above Baton Rouge, the Coast Guard said.
Swirling currents from the rushing floodwaters will continue to make shipping difficult for several weeks in the lower section of the river, officials said.
"It's dropping slowly now," a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers spokesman said. "This is really going to be a slow descent."
The Army Corps of Engineers plans to begin closing bays in the Bonnet Carre Spillway on Tuesday or Wednesday, he said. The bays had been opened to divert floodwaters.
Crews over the weekend righted a barge containing a volatile mix of benzene and gasoline that overturned March 17, slowing shipping along the river past Baton Rouge.
The barge accident was one of several on the lower Mississippi over the past two weeks as the river was swollen to its fourth-highest level this century with flood waters from the Ohio Valley.
